content.name: p
children: Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) is, by far, the most popular authentication and message security method used on webhook requests, including 65% of the webhooks we studied. In this method, the webhook provider and listener use a secret key to sign and validate webhook requests.

children.name: p
children: On webhook requests, the provider signs the webhook message using the secret key plus a hashing algorithm — typically
, and then includes the signature in the webhook request as a header.

children.name: p
children: The webhook listener receives the request and repeats the same steps — signs and encodes the webhook message using the secret key — and compares the resulting signature with the value sent in the request header. If the result matches, the request is considered legitimate.

children.name: li
children: : Assuming the secret key is known only by the webhook provider and the listener, the HMAC process verifies that the message comes from the webhook provider (authenticity) and its contents are the same as they were at the time of sending (integrity).

children.name: li
children: In HMAC, secret keys are not sent with the webhook request — only the signatures created with it — reducing the risk of stolen keys.

children: HMAC is only as good as its implementation

content.name: p
children: Like any other security control, HMAC is only as good as its implementation.
